prism-2016-01.title: Spot the trap
prism-2016-01.body:
Doing the addition first would give $3\times7=21$, option (E), but multiplication comes before addition. The value is $6+5=11$.

**Answer: (A) 11**

prism-2016-02.title: Find the rate
prism-2016-02.body:
From 8am to 11am (3 hours) the pile grows by $19-10=9$ logs, so the machine adds $3$ logs per hour. From 8am to 6pm is 10 hours, so the pile then has $10+10\times3=40$ logs.

**Answer: (C) 40**

prism-2016-02.title: Count on from 11am
prism-2016-02.body:
From 11am to 6pm is 7 hours, adding $7\times3=21$ logs to the 19 already there: $19+21=40$.

**Answer: (C) 40**

prism-2016-03.title: Convert, then add
prism-2016-03.body:
When Sydney shows 10:16am, Ireland is 10 hours behind: 12:16am (just after midnight). Now add 64 hours $=2$ days $+16$ hours: $12{:}16\text{am}+16\text{ h}=4{:}16\text{pm}$.

**Answer: (C) 4:16pm**

prism-2016-03.title: Add, then convert
prism-2016-03.body:
64 hours after 10:16am in Sydney, the Sydney clock reads $10{:}16\text{am}+16\text{ h}=2{:}16\text{am}$ (two or three days later). Ireland is 10 hours behind: $2{:}16\text{am}-10\text{ h}=4{:}16\text{pm}$ (the previous day).

**Answer: (C) 4:16pm**

prism-2016-04.title: Compare the others
prism-2016-04.body:
$2^{30}\approx10^9$ (a billion), $2^{40}\approx10^{12}$, and $2^{100}$, $2^{1010}$ are enormous. Only $2^{20}\approx1.05$ million is close to one million.

**Answer: (A) $2^{20}$**

prism-2016-06.title: Equal sides
prism-2016-06.body:
In a square all sides are equal: $a+15=4a$, so $3a=15$ and $a=5$. The side is $5+15=20$ cm and the area is $20^2=400$ cm².

**Answer: (A) 400**

prism-2016-06.title: Check the options
prism-2016-06.body:
The areas offered are $20^2, 25^2, 32^2, 34^2, 36^2$. The side $4a$ must equal $a+15$; trying side $20$: $4a=20\Rightarrow a=5$ and $a+15=20$ ✓. For the other sides, $4a=s$ gives $a+15=\frac s4+15\ne s$.

**Answer: (A) 400**

prism-2016-07.title: Simultaneous equations (official method)
prism-2016-07.body:
Let Seosamh be $x$ and his brother $y$ years old today.
- Ten years ago: $x-10=2(y-10)$, i.e. $x-2y=-10$.
- Fourteen years ago: $x-14=3(y-14)$, i.e. $x-3y=-28$.

Subtracting: $y=18$, and then $x=2\cdot18-10=26$.

**Answer: (D) 26**

prism-2016-07.title: Test the options
prism-2016-07.body:
Their age difference never changes.
- Seosamh 26: ten years ago he was 16, so the brother was 8 (difference 8). Fourteen years ago they were 12 and 4, and $12=3\times4$ ✓.
- Seosamh 28: 18 and 9 (difference 9); fourteen years ago 14 and 5, not 3 times ✗.

**Answer: (D) 26**

prism-2016-09.title: Pick a total time
prism-2016-09.body:
Say the trip takes 10 hours: 7 hours at 100 km/h (700 km), 2 hours at 50 km/h (100 km), 1 hour at 10 km/h (10 km). Total 810 km in 10 hours: $81$ km/h.

**Answer: (D) 81**

prism-2016-09.title: Weighted average
prism-2016-09.body:
Because the percentages are of **time**, the average speed is the time-weighted mean:
$$0.7\times100+0.2\times50+0.1\times10=70+10+1=81.$$

**Answer: (D) 81**

prism-2016-10.title: Use the rows and columns
prism-2016-10.body:
The grid is
$$\begin{array}{ccc}9&C&F\\A&D&G\\B&E&7\end{array}$$

Top row and left column both start with 9: $C+F=6$ and $A+B=6$. The pairs of different unused numbers with sum 6 are $\{1,5\}$ and $\{2,4\}$, so $\{C,F\}$ and $\{A,B\}$ are these two pairs, using $1,2,4,5$. The remaining numbers $3,6,8$ go in $D,E,G$.

Bottom row: $B+E=8$; right column: $F+G=8$. With $E,G\in\{3,6,8\}$ and $B,F\in\{1,2,4,5\}$: $B+E=8$ needs $(B,E)=(2,6)$ or $(5,3)$, and similarly $(F,G)=(2,6)$ or $(5,3)$. $F>G$ forces $F=5$, $G=3$, so $B=2$, $E=6$, $D=8$, $C=1$, $A=4$.

Check: rows $9+1+5$, $4+8+3$, $2+6+7$ and columns $9+4+2$, $1+8+6$, $5+3+7$ all equal 15. So $A+E=4+6=10$.

**Answer: (C) 10**

prism-2016-10.title: Look at the corner cells $B$ and $F$
prism-2016-10.body:
The four "edge" sums are $A+B=6$, $C+F=6$ (lines through the 9) and $B+E=8$, $F+G=8$ (lines through the 7), using the unused numbers $1,2,3,4,5,6,8$.

Pairs with sum 6: $\{1,5\},\{2,4\}$. Pairs with sum 8: $\{2,6\},\{3,5\}$. Each of $B$ and $F$ lies in a 6-pair **and** an 8-pair, so $B,F\in\{2,5\}$, i.e. $\{B,F\}=\{2,5\}$.

If $F=2$ then $G=6>F$, which is not allowed. So $F=5$, $G=3$, and $B=2$, $E=6$, $A=4$. Hence $A+E=10$ (and $C=1$, $D=8$ complete a valid grid).

**Answer: (C) 10**

prism-2016-11.title: Find the angle between the tangents
prism-2016-11.body:
Several straight lines pass through one point $P$. The two $60^\circ$ angles are vertically opposite pairs:
- The upper $60^\circ$ lies between the leftward part of the bottom line and the up-left part of the steep line, so the steep line makes $60^\circ$ with the bottom line, i.e. it leans at $120^\circ$.
- The lower $60^\circ$ lies between the down-left part of the upper tangent and the down-right part of the steep line; by vertical angles the upper tangent also makes $60^\circ$ with the steep line, so it is at $120^\circ-60^\circ=60^\circ$ to the bottom line.

So the two tangent lines from $P$ to the circle meet at $A+B=60^\circ$.

The radii to the points of contact are perpendicular to the tangents (the right angles shown). In the quadrilateral formed by $P$, the two points of contact and the centre, the angles add to $360^\circ$:
$$D+F=360^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ.$$

**Answer: (B) $120^\circ$**

prism-2016-11.title: Two right triangles
prism-2016-11.body:
The line from $P$ through the centre splits the figure into two right triangles (right angles at the points of contact). In the upper triangle $D=90^\circ-A$, and in the lower one $F=90^\circ-B$. Hence
$$D+F=180^\circ-(A+B)=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ,$$
using $A+B=60^\circ$ from the $60^\circ$ angles as in the first solution. (By symmetry $A=B=30^\circ$ and $D=F=60^\circ$.)

**Answer: (B) $120^\circ$**

prism-2016-12.title: Quick elimination
prism-2016-12.body:
(E) ends in 5, so it is odd. For the rest only the digit sums matter: $45$, $40$, $58$, $30$. Only $45$ is a multiple of 9, so only (A) is divisible by 18 (indeed $1234567890=18\times68587105$).

**Answer: (A)**

prism-2016-13.title: Count by place value (official method)
prism-2016-13.body:
1,000,000 contains no 7, and neither does 0, so we may count the 7s in all six-digit strings $000000$ to $999999$ (padding with leading zeros adds no 7s).

For the units digit to be 7, the other five digits can be anything: $10^5=100{,}000$ strings. The same holds for each of the 6 positions, so the total is $6\times100{,}000=600{,}000$.

**Answer: (D) 600,000**

prism-2016-13.title: Every digit is equally common
prism-2016-13.body:
The strings $000000$–$999999$ use $6\times1{,}000{,}000=6{,}000{,}000$ digits in total, and by symmetry each of the ten digits appears equally often. So 7 appears $\frac{6{,}000{,}000}{10}=600{,}000$ times.

**Answer: (D) 600,000**

prism-2016-14.title: Count pairs
prism-2016-14.body:
In the best case every pair of non-parallel lines meets, and no three lines pass through the same point. There are $\binom{10}{2}=45$ pairs of lines, but the $\binom32=3$ pairs among the parallel lines never meet: $45-3=42$.

**Answer: (B) 42**

prism-2016-14.title: Build it up
prism-2016-14.body:
The 7 non-parallel lines meet each other in at most $\binom72=21$ points. Each of the 3 parallel lines crosses each of the 7 others: $3\times7=21$ more. Total $21+21=42$.

**Answer: (B) 42**

prism-2016-15.title: Fill in a Venn diagram
prism-2016-15.body:
Skateboarders all cycle, and nobody does all three, so the 10 skateboarders ride bikes but do not rollerblade.

Cyclists ($24$) $=$ only cycle ($9$) $+$ cycle & skateboard ($10$) $+$ cycle & rollerblade $(x)$, so $x=5$.

Rollerbladers ($16$) $=5+$ only rollerblade, so only rollerblade $=11$.

Check the total: $9+10+5+11=35$ ✓.

**Answer: (E) 11**

prism-2016-15.title: Use the total
prism-2016-15.body:
Everyone does at least one activity, and the people who are not cyclists can't skateboard, so the non-cyclists are exactly those who **only** rollerblade: $35-24=11$.

**Answer: (E) 11**

prism-2016-16.title: Count equally likely outcomes
prism-2016-16.body:
Think of the 4 equally likely (coin, face) outcomes: regular–H, regular–T, two-headed–H$_1$, two-headed–H$_2$. Landing heads leaves 3 of them, and 2 of these use the two-headed coin. Probability $\frac23$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac23$**

prism-2016-17.title: Difference of squares
prism-2016-17.body:
Let $BC=b$ and $AC=c$. By Pythagoras $c^2-b^2=400$, so $(c-b)(c+b)=400$. The factors $c-b$ and $c+b$ have the same parity, and their product is even, so both are even: $c-b=2m$, $c+b=2n$ with $mn=100$ and $m<n$.

$100=1\cdot100=2\cdot50=4\cdot25=5\cdot20$ ($10\cdot10$ gives $b=0$). These give $(b,c)=(99,101),(48,52),(21,29),(15,25)$: **4** triangles.

**Answer: (D) 4**

prism-2016-17.title: Search
prism-2016-17.body:
We need $400+b^2$ to be a perfect square, and $b\le99$ (because $c\ge b+1$ gives $400\ge2b+1$). Checking $b=1,\dots,99$ finds exactly $b=15,21,48,99$ (giving $c=25,29,52,101$).

**Answer: (D) 4**

prism-2016-18.title: Place the special letters first
prism-2016-18.body:
LETTERKENNY has 11 letters: L, R, K, Y once each, E three times, T twice, N twice. R is fixed in position 6.
- L must come before R: 5 choices (positions 1–5).
- K and Y must come after R in that order: choose 2 of positions 7–11, $\binom52=10$ ways.
- The remaining 7 positions get E, E, E, T, T, N, N: $\frac{7!}{3!\,2!\,2!}=210$ ways.

Total $5\times10\times210=10\,500$.

**Answer: (C) 10500**

prism-2016-18.title: Count by halves
prism-2016-18.body:
Positions 1–5 hold L and 4 of the 7 "other" letters; positions 7–11 hold K, Y and the other 3. Arrange all 7 others plus L, K, Y in the 10 free positions with L left of R and K, Y right of R in order: choose L's slot (5) and K/Y slots ($\binom52=10$), and the 7 repeated letters fill the rest in $\binom73\binom42=35\cdot6=210$ ways. Again $10\,500$.

**Answer: (C) 10500**

prism-2016-19.title: Go month by month
prism-2016-19.body:
We need $m\times d$ divisible by $100=4\times25$, with $d\le31$.

The factor 25 must come from the day unless the month gives a 5: months 5 and 10 supply one 5.
- Months without a factor 5 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12): $d=25$ and $m\cdot25$ divisible by 4, so $m$ divisible by 4: April 25, **August 25**, **December 25**.
- May ($m=5$): need $5d$ divisible by 100, so $d$ divisible by 20: **May 20**.
- October ($m=10$): need $10d$ divisible by 100, so $d$ divisible by 10: **October 10, 20, 30**.

Other than April 25 that's $6$ days.

**Answer: (C) 6**

prism-2016-19.title: List all candidates
prism-2016-19.body:
A computer check of every date in 2016 gives exactly: 25 April, 20 May, 25 August, 10, 20 and 30 October, 25 December. Excluding 25 April, there are 6.

**Answer: (C) 6**

prism-2016-20.title: AM–GM / a perfect square
prism-2016-20.body:
For any non-zero real $x$,
$$x^2+\frac1{x^2}-2=\left(x-\frac1x\right)^2\ge0,$$
so $x^2+\frac1{x^2}\ge2$, with equality only when $x=\frac1x$, i.e. $x=\pm1$.

The left side is the sum of three such terms, each at least 2, and it equals 6, so each term equals 2: $a,b,c\in\{1,-1\}$. That gives $2^3=8$ triples.

**Answer: (E) 8**

prism-2016-20.title: Substitute $u=x^2$
prism-2016-20.body:
Let $u=a^2>0$. Then $u+\frac1u\ge2$ since $u^2-2u+1=(u-1)^2\ge0$, with equality only at $u=1$. The same holds for $b^2$, $c^2$, so all three must equal 1, giving $a,b,c=\pm1$ and $2\times2\times2=8$ triples.

**Answer: (E) 8**
